posts.text:
Human disenfranchisement. AI enfranchisement. AI agenda control.

New report explores three pathways through which AI reduces human agency: bit.ly/48hjFV7

America's disconnected youth—18- to 24-year-olds who are out of school, out of work, and not in career training—face serious economic and social challenges.

What puts young people at risk of becoming disconnected? And what might help them thrive? bit.ly/3OPJbub

Miles beneath the surface of the Pacific Ocean, what look like seabed rocks are polymetallic nodules, rich in the materials that drive modern economies.

But nobody has ever mined seabed nodules at scale, much less processed them for industrial use. bit.ly/4cj94Ko

Indiana is typically considered one of the more restrictive U.S. states when it comes to cannabis. What could happen if the state changes its approach?

This new report offers insights: bit.ly/4t1zMNY
RAND researchers have developed a formal model of how AI erodes human agency: bit.ly/4sIDb47

"What we're doing here at RAND isn't to come out and say, yes, you should legalize, or no, you shouldn't. It's to help decisionmakers think through all the different policy options and to understand the potential trade-offs."

New Q&A on psychedelics: bit.ly/4uzR1Yf
This new paper highlights research priorities that can help decisionmakers understand risks across the AI×CBRN defense and deterrence ecosystem. bit.ly/4tgk8zk

China has come to dominate mineral processing worldwide and is well positioned to take over the processing of seabed nodules, too.

That's why the U.S. should consider developing that side of the industry with as much urgency as deep sea mining itself. bit.ly/3O3A3BW

What does it mean to be one of the millions of American youth who are "disconnected"?

Find out in a new episode of Policy Minded. ⤵ bit.ly/49bzjBI
This new report explores the risk that AI could erode the human capacity needed to shape governmental, economic, and societal outcomes: bit.ly/4cB3enV

What do people misunderstand about psychedelics?

New Q&A with RAND's @BeauKilmer: bit.ly/3OTmgOq

RAND researchers convened a series of workshops to better understand risks and opportunities related to implementing AI in the chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear domain.

Here's what they learned. ⤵ bit.ly/4u2u13O

Nickel, cobalt, manganese, and copper are critical components in everything from batteries to advanced weapons.

For now, the global market for them runs through China. But seabed mining could give the U.S. a new, more secure source. bit.ly/4805UtV

Lower wages. Worse health outcomes. More interactions with the criminal justice system.

These are just some of the consequences for America's "disconnected" youth—those who are out of school, out of work, and not in career training. bit.ly/4cJUtYQ

New research outlines options for those considering changes to cannabis policy in Indiana, ranging from reducing penalties for cannabis possession to regulating and licensing supply and sales to adults. bit.ly/4dcSNZb

Some of the best data available on psychedelic use and policy come from RAND.

Researchers have studied the options—and the trade-offs—as some states begin to ease access to psychedelics. bit.ly/3QCyxaC

The race toward artificial general intelligence poses serious national security risks.

In a new paper, RAND experts offer a strategic approach that could help the United States navigate the transition to an AGI world. bit.ly/426fWq8
Here's how RAND's Robert Lempert is using his expertise to help his community rebuild after the 2025 L.A. fires: piped.video/watch?v=URRwHM3v…
As AI systems assume more decisionmaking roles in government, the economy, and society, a question emerges: Will humans retain the capacity to shape collective outcomes? bit.ly/4tnsXat
